recipes.name: Easy Peach Cobbler with Cake Mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Spread peach slices evenly in the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Stir water and sugar together in a small bowl until dissolved; pour mixture over peaches. Sprinkle cinnamon over peaches, then cake mix. Top cake mix with pats of cream cheese, then butter.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Peach Cobbler with Cake Mix
raw_recipe.description: This fresh peach cobbler made with cake mix and cream cheese couldn't be easier to make! Delight everyone at the table with this decadent dessert.

review.reviewBody:
I've used this recipe for years and it's always been great. Well, with a few changes it works out great.

First, skip the extra sugar if your peaches are already sweet (most fresh ones are if they're ripe and ALL canned peaches are sweet enough). If you're using another fruit, like blackberries or raspberries, then you'd need the extra sugar. Remember, the cake mix has sugar, too.

Second, cream the cheese and cake mix together with a pastry cutter or a couple forks until it resembles a crumbly granola-type consistency.

Third, melt the butter and pour it over with the liquid (use less liquid if your fruit is really juicy!) Alternately, cream the butter in with the cheese and cake mix (see above).

And last--cinnamon is not always appropriate if you are using this with a different fruit. Other options that might sound better to you are nutmeg, vanilla bean specs or vanilla-flavored sugar. Oh, and for a crunchy bonus, sprinkle the top with sliced almonds before baking.

OK, I reviewed this before but last night 8/26/07 I made this again and found a better way to make the cobbler. I mixed the cream cheese with the cake mix in a food processor just until mixture gets crumbly. After putting this mixture on the peaches (used fresh this time) I added the butter (melted) over the top of the cobbler. My fiance said that was the best cobbler I have ever made. I give the credit to my food processor. This recipe is now 5 stars!

GREAT recipe, Rebecca! This is absolutely DELICIOUS AND EASY! I love to cook & bake & am always on the lookout for a great recipes using ingredients I have on hand..& this one is a hands-down WINNER!

I buttered the glass casserole dish. I didn't have fresh peaches so I used 2 large cans of peaches in heavy syrup. I dissolved 3 TB of cornstarch into 3 TB cold water & then added it to the syrup with one teaspoon of vanilla & 3 TB of brown sugar, & simmered it in a sauce pan until fairly thick (about 10 min), constantly stirring. I then poured about one cup of the mixture over the peaches. I worked the cubed cold butter & cubed cold cream cheese together with the yellow cake mix in a large bowl until crumbly (only takes about 5 minutes.) Then I brushed the top with melted butter & sprinkled with extra cinnamon before baking for 50+ minutes, keeping an eye on the topping to make sure it didn't burn. Baking it a little longer keeps the bottom of the crust from being soggy & firms up & crisps the crust a little better. The juice-ratio was perfect b/c it was thickened.

The topping will soften overnight so for leftovers, I put the cobbler back into the oven on 350 for about 10-15 minutes. Perfect!

I've already passed this revised recipe along to several friends after taking it to a family party. I'll make this many, many more years to come and try out different fruits & cake mix flavor. YUM!

When I started making this my boyfriend and i kinda had a little argument because he did not believe that this was really peach cobbler, because of how little the ingredients were. But , during the baking time I truly thought it was going to turn out runny and the crust just not right. I used canned peaches and the syrup instead of sugar and water, and I had to bake it a alot longer then 45 minutes, but the end result was incredible. It thickened up just perfect after letting it sit for about an hour after baking. My boyfriend totally apologized and thought it was delicious ( which it was). This was my first time baking a peach cobbler and want to thank you for a great recipe. It was easy and turned out Perfect. Thank you!!

I had fresh peaches,and very little gluten free flour,so I found this recipe to make for a family gathering. I am happy to report that this conbler got rave reviews! 
I have gluten free diets in my family,and I poted for a gluten free yellow cake mix. I followed another reviewer advice and processed the cream cheese and cake mix in my Ninja blender which was way much easier then blending the mixture with a hand pastry cutter. I also did not add water, or sugar to my already sweet rippened peaches,too much water would have been a disaster! I am looking forward to trying this recipe with other fruits,rather it be fresh,frozen or even canned.

Minor changes and clarification of instructions:

-drained canned peaches in bottom (*Doubled the Peaches -two 29oz. Cans- one heavy syrup/ one in juice, Drain peaches- keep juice).
-Pour 1 cup of peach juice over peaches.
-sprinkle cinnamon over peaches
- pour cake/Cream cheese mixture (*Blend cake mix with room temperature cream cheese).
- pour butter on top of cream cheese/cake mixture.
-Bake 

*Used Dunkin Hines Butter Cake in box.

There were a few flaws to this recipe as written, but it really doesn't matter because it tastes amazing. The cake mix/cream cheese combo is delectable. And using high-quality peaches definitely helps.

First of all, 12 peaches is a LOT of peaches. I used 10 peaches in a standard 9x13 casserole dish, and that was quite enough. I also used a slightly smaller size of cake mix.

An easy peeling method for peaches: boil the peach in water for 30 seconds, then put it in ice water for 10 seconds. The skin should basically slide right off. They do need to be at least slightly ripe for this method to work. 

Like others, I mixed the cream cheese and cake mix together before baking, and i melted the butter before drizzling it on top.

My one criticism of the dish is that it was very runny. A full cup of water is probably not necessary. I'd go with 1/2 c water and sugar next time.

LOVE IT!!! I make this often, at several people's requests. I use 2 large cans peaches. Definitely cut the cream cheese into cake mix using 2 knives instead of laying on top. Then melt butter & drizzle evenly all over top. I prefer to use a little more cinnamon. Had to cook a bit longer than what directions said.

Made it as written, I used canned peaches in Heavy Syrup instead of fresh ones. Used one cup of the reserve liquid from the peaches. I also cut the butter and cream cheese into the cake mix. When I placed the cake mix on top of the peaches I gently pushed the batter into the peaches so that it could absorb the liquid from the peaches while it baked. Cooked it in a 350 degree convection oven on the middle rack for 55 mins until it was golden brown. Came out perfect. there was no excess liquid since the cake mix absorbed all the liquid.

It just went into the oven! Great recipe. I don't like sugar so I used a low sugar mix which was still too sweet. I used half cream cheese and half sour cream and it was still a little too sweet. Next time I will omit the cream cheese and use just all sour cream , I added a little nutmeg and allspice the cinnamon and used lite brown sugar. It looks delicious. Next week I will try it with different fruits.
I mixed the butter and cream cheese with the cake mix until crumbly then dropped all over the top of the cobbler. The topping was uniform in texture and better tasting.
It came out so good! I will make it again!❤️
I used a gluten free cake mix and my mixer to incorporate the cream cheese, just stopping before it started to come together. Delicious! Husband pleaser!

I tweaked the recipe from recommendations. I mixed the cake mix and softened cream cheese . Also, I used fresh blueberries with the canned peaches. No extra sugar . The sweetness from the peaches was enough. It was a fit with the family

I made this a few daus ago and used canned peaches in 100% juice and a yellow cake mix since it says you can do that. I did as others suggested and blended the cream cheese with the cake mix and melted the butter and poured over the mix. This was plenty sweet without adding additional sugar, and I had plenty of fluid with just using the peach juice. The flavor was nice, but I wasnt crazy about the texture of the cake mix portion. I just prefer a true cobbler, so I will not make this again. It was however extremely easy.
I've made this twice with peaches, now I'm making it with freshly canned blackberries. I omitted the sugar and water each time b/c of the sugar in the syrups. Delish, a definite keeper
instructions are too vague. Is the box cake mix made up according to box instructions or is the powder from dry cake just poured over the water and peaches. This is just awful recipe writing
followed directions exactly. what a mess! never again
No changes. Absolutely scrumptious!
